text:
jordan: FYI customer (Acme) opened a support case — after we rotated an ephemeral service token their engineers can still hit the API but the console shows 403 when switching to the project. They can see org-level items but project page says "You do not have permission". Repro steps attached.

maya: tagging SRE and assigning. can you paste the repro & any headers/logs? @sre-oncall :eyes:

alex: quick Q — is this the ephemeral token from the new short-lived credential flow or a service key rotation?

jordan: it's the short-lived flow (ephemeral). repro from their side: 
1) web console -> auth via SSO (ok)
2) switch org -> works
3) switch project -> 403 shown in UI
4) curl the same project list endpoint with the ephemeral token they used: 
```
GET /api/v1/projects
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... (ephemeral)
Response: 403 {"error":"permission_denied","detail":"missing project:viewer"}
```

They ran `curl --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects` and got 403, but `POST /v1/generate` using same token worked and returned 200.

support-bot: Ticket #67890 created and linked to thread. Priority set to P1 by customer.

maya: interesting — token is valid for model calls but not project listing. suggests token scope or bound roles differ between endpoints. do we have token introspect logs? @alex can you check token binding record?

alex: pulled introspect for the ephemeral id `ephemeral_abc123` — claims show scopes: ["inference:run","org:read"], but no `project:read` claim. Looks like the ephemeral mint step didn't attach project-level role claim.

jordan: customer says this only started after we rotated the upstream service that mints ephemeral tokens (we rolled the minting service yesterday).

alex: root cause hypothesis: the minting service now fetches identity from the service principal which lost its project binding during the rotation (the service principal key rotation created a new principal reference that we didn't propagate role bindings for). Because project access is derived from the minting principal's bindings, the ephemeral tokens are missing project claims.

maya: repro on our end: spin up ephemeral token via mint endpoint using the rotated principal -> reproduce 403 on project endpoints, but inference endpoints return 200. confirmed.

sre-oncall: action items:
- immediate workaround: rebind the original project role to the minting principal (or grant `project:viewer` to the newly rotated principal). this will restore project claims for freshly minted tokens.
- mid-term: add a validation step in the rotation workflow to copy role bindings to new principals and fail rotation if missing.
- also add an automated smoke test: mint ephemeral token then call `GET /v1/projects` as part of deploy.

jordan: customer applied the temporary `project:viewer` binding to their minting principal and confirmed console access is restored. They want a postmortem and a durable fix.

maya: thanks — I'll draft the postmortem and the rotation checklist. Alex, can you open an infra PR to add the binding-copy and smoke test?

alex: already on it, PR in progress. adding unit test + integration smoke.

jordan: notes for support reply to customer: apologize, explain root cause (rotation lost project binding -> ephemeral tokens lacked project claim -> console & project-listing 403), document workaround (rebind minting principal with `project:viewer` or re-run rotation with binding-copy), ETA for fix (we'll push rotation-check + smoke test in next 48h).

maya: closing loop — i'll post the postmortem link here when ready and update the ticket. :white_check_mark:
